candidates.rationale: The exact `&mut &'a [T]` input requires modeling both the returned first element and the updated slice view. Current Verus lowering materializes the inner shared slice as unsized `[T]` when tracking the mutable reference, so no valid contract can express the observable post-state.

The exact `&mut &'a [T]` input requires modeling both the returned last element and the updated slice view. Current Verus lowering materializes the inner shared slice as unsized `[T]` when tracking the mutable reference, so no valid contract can express the observable post-state.

Success and the returned middle subslice depend on both `SlicePattern::as_slice` values. Vstd has no semantic model for `SlicePattern`, so neither the `Option` discriminant nor the selected subrange can be determined.

The source compares the leading subslice with `prefix.as_slice()`, but vstd does not model `SlicePattern::as_slice`. A suffix-only postcondition would leave success and the removed length undetermined.

The source compares the trailing subslice with `suffix.as_slice()`, but vstd does not model `SlicePattern::as_slice`. A prefix-only postcondition would leave success and the removed length undetermined.

The result is determined by pointer addresses, alignment, element size, and allocation provenance, which slice views erase. Vstd also lacks a model for `core::range::Range`, so no useful deterministic contract exists in current vocabulary.
